A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GoLU research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original activation-function experiments across vision and language tasks, training-dynamics analyses, timing measurements and an appendix experiment on learning-curve extrapolation.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Flipped Mish evaluations, further instance-segmentation experiments and WMT14 English–German translation results.

M1.justification: The GoLU formula and reported training/inference procedure remain unchanged. Appendix B adds an auxiliary activation, Flipped Mish, defined as x[1 − tanh(softplus(−x))], by reflecting Mish's underlying distribution. This is a distinct method addition supporting the existing GoLU investigation.

E1.justification: Appendix I adds WMT14 English–German machine translation with approximately 4.5 million training pairs. This introduces bilingual sequence-to-sequence prediction and German-language coverage beyond the existing language-modeling tasks. All earlier vision datasets and the learning-curve extrapolation task remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds FMish to comparisons on ImageNet-1k with ResNet-18, ResNet-50 and ViT-B/32, explicitly comparing its results with GoLU and the Table 2 baselines. The six established baseline activations remain unchanged; the translation experiment uses that existing comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a Transformer-Big translation protocol with 50 training epochs, beam-search decoding and BLEU4 evaluation, and adds a seven-learning-rate Mask R-CNN evaluation. It also changes the stated loss-landscape evaluation from a test-data batch in v1 Appendix B to the full CIFAR-10 test set in v2 Appendix C. That last change establishes a reported protocol revision, without establishing whether the experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: v1 only conjectured that learning-rate adjustment could improve Mask R-CNN results; v2 supplies Box and Mask mAP sensitivity studies in Figures 12–13. Appendix B adds FMish experiments probing right-skewed gating, and Appendix C adds quantitative loss-distribution and variance analysis. Earlier learning-rate studies, critical-difference analysis and the negative LC-PFN case study remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report three training seeds, means with standard errors, and the same critical-difference analysis at alpha = 0.05. Added experiments follow the existing reporting practice. Table 7 changes standard-error values without documenting a different estimator or run count; the new landscape variances describe perturbation sensitivity.

E6.justification: New results include FMish ImageNet accuracies of 70.73, 76.20 and 75.67 for ResNet-18, ResNet-50 and ViT-B/32, respectively, and translation BLEU4 scores of 28.44±0.15 for GoLU versus 28.34±0.08 for Swish. Table 7 adds learning-rate-0.03 results, including GoLU Box/Mask mAP of 39.36/34.97, and revises its existing learning-rate-0.02 standard errors from 0.001/0.001 to 0.101/0.083 while retaining the means. Figure 9 adds landscape-variance results. Tables 1–6 and 8–9 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: v2 adds a formal point-symmetry definition and derives Var[f(X)] ≈ f'(mu)^2 sigma^2 using a Taylor expansion under smoothness and localized-input assumptions. Appendix B also derives the reflected gate and formally defines FMish. These are localized mathematical additions; the original GoLU definition, derivative identities and gate-tail asymptotic remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contribution: GoLU uses Gompertz asymmetry to reduce activation variance, support favorable training dynamics and provide broadly competitive performance at comparable computational cost. The added experiments support these retained claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly interprets FMish's performance through right-skewed gating, its slope at zero and its negative-tail behavior. Section 3.6 replaces a learning-rate conjecture with an assertion that 0.03 improves all activations, although Table 7 contradicts that generalization, including ReLU Box mAP decreasing from 38.33 to 38.25. Existing non-universality caveats and the LC-PFN negative result remain.

D1.justification: Appendix G newly discloses NVIDIA A100 usage and approximately 112K GPU hours, with TinyViT using an H100 for 455 GPU hours. Appendix I documents the translation architecture, optimizer, schedule, gradient accumulation and L40S runtime of roughly 1750 GPU hours. Earlier implementation details, relative timing results and the code-access link remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ott et al. (2019) for Fairseq in the translation experiment. Appendix B also extends the substantive relationship to Mish through the reflected-distribution construction. The existing references and broader positioning among self-gated activations remain.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include localized explanations and cross-references, new appendix sections, a dedicated Test Loss Curves section, and affiliation and acknowledgement updates. There is no extensive rewriting of the central narrative.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the displays: activation, gate and derivative panels are recombined into Figures 1–2, and the nine main-text training-curve figures move to enlarged displays in Appendix H. Figure 5 is redrawn, Table 7 gains learning-rate columns, and new FMish, loss-density, instance-segmentation heatmaps and translation-table displays are added. Many other plots are retained unchanged despite renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the evidence by testing v1's Mask R-CNN learning-rate conjecture, adding a targeted FMish comparison and translation evaluation, and documenting mathematical assumptions and compute resources. These provide useful incremental support and transparency. The gains are tempered by the new claim of improvement across all activations contradicting Table 7, and by translation differences that are small relative to the reported standard errors.
